issues.description: finalize() complects four concerns into one mutating loop: ref-merging, parent-chain refinement subtraction, $defs de-duplication, and $ref propagation
issues.detail: flattenRef now does (a) inherit-from-ref, (b) restore child overrides, (c) strip parent-only keys on a 'refinement' branch, (d) JSON.stringify-diff to delete keys that match the extracted definition, and (e) propagate $ref from parent to child. These are five different transformations on the same mutable map, sequenced by side effect. The control flow ('if isParentRef' vs 'if refSchema.$ref' vs 'if seen.parent && seen.parent !== ref') is the place where the bug will live. This is COMPLECTED. A simple version would compute the final schema as a pure function of (own props, inherited props, parent ref, child overrides) and assign once at the end.

issues.description: JSON.stringify used as a value-equality primitive for de-duplication
issues.detail: Two places now do `JSON.stringify(schema[key]) === JSON.stringify(refSeen.def![key])` to decide whether to delete a key. This is place-oriented thinking applied to values: you have actual values, but you're comparing their string serializations, which is order-sensitive, undefined-sensitive, and silently wrong on anything containing a function, Date, RegExp, or property-order difference. The right tool is a structural-equality function over the value domain you actually have (JSON Schema fragments). Using stringify here is EASY-NOT-SIMPLE and will produce a heisenbug the first time a processor adds keys in a different order.

issues.description: Seen.ref is overloaded as three different things: 'inherit from', 'parent in clone chain', and 'already processed' sentinel (null)
issues.detail: The same field encodes (1) 'inherit JSON Schema props from this schema' (set by processor), (2) fallback to parent when processor didn't set it, and (3) a null-sentinel meaning 'I've been visited, don't recurse'. The PR adds a separate `parent` field to disentangle (1) and (2), which is the right instinct, but then keeps the null-sentinel inside `ref` AND adds a second use of `parent` in the propagation block. The identity (what does this slot mean today) is now ambiguous and changes during the traversal. Either model the state as an explicit phase enum / visited-set, or split into three named fields: `inheritFrom`, `cloneParent`, `visited`. This is the classic value/identity/time complecting.

issues.description: The 'override count went from 6 to 12' test change is a behavior change disguised as a test update
issues.detail: Previously overrides skipped `isParent` schemas; now they run on everyone. That's why the count doubled. This may be the right behavior, but the diff treats it as a mechanical number change with no comment in the test explaining *why* every parent in the chain now gets its override called. If a user has a counter or a logger in their override (as the test itself demonstrates), this is an observable breaking change. The PR description does not mention it. At minimum, document why `isParent` no longer gates overrides, and consider whether running override twice (once on parent, once on child-refinement) is actually what callers want.

issues.description: The refinement-detection heuristic `(zodSchema as any)._zod.parent === ref` is incidental coupling between finalize and the constructor's `{ parent: true }` flag
issues.detail: The classic schemas.ts change adds `{ parent: true }` to the clone call so that finalize can later say 'oh, this clone is a refinement of its parent, strip parent-only keys'. The signaling channel is: constructor sets `_zod.parent`, process() copies it to `seen.parent`, finalize() asks `_zod.parent === ref` to decide pruning. That's three hops where the meaning ('this is a check-refinement, not a structural derivative') is implicit. A named value on the seen entry — e.g. `seen.relationship: 'refinement' | 'wrapper' | 'inherited'` — set once at process time, would make finalize a pure dispatch on that value instead of a re-derivation.

issues.description: play.ts committed with project-local debug scaffolding and a relative import into src
issues.detail: play.ts switched from `import * as z from 'zod/v4'` to `import * as z from './packages/zod/src/index.js'` and contains hand-written console.log probes for the bug being fixed. This is hammock-thinking left in the keyboard: useful while debugging, but shipping it conflates 'the published package surface' with 'my local repro'. Either delete before merge, move under a tests/repros/ folder, or convert to a real test. It does not belong at repo root in the merged commit.

issues.description: The mini-schemas change is a commented-out line being uncommented with no explanation
issues.detail: `mini/schemas.ts` previously had `// { parent: true }` commented out; the PR uncomments it. That suggests someone tried this before, backed it out, and now we're trying it again. The reason it was commented out is not captured anywhere in the diff. Worth a sentence in the commit or a code comment so the next person doesn't re-disable it for the same forgotten reason.

issues.description: fileProcessor refactor is a good simplification but worth naming the invariant
issues.detail: The change from 'put shared props in every anyOf branch' to 'hoist shared props to root, leave only the discriminating contentMediaType in anyOf' is genuinely simpler and the snapshot diff confirms it. This is the kind of decomposition the rest of the PR should aspire to: identify the value (shared file constraints) vs the variant (per-mime contentMediaType), put each in its own place. Worth a one-line comment naming that invariant so a future contributor doesn't 'helpfully' put the shared props back into each branch.

review.summary: The fix addresses a real bug — metadata and $ref propagation across clone chains — and the instinct to split `ref` (inherit-from) from `parent` (clone-chain) is correct. But the implementation pays for it by adding complexity in finalize(): five different transformations now run as a sequence of mutations on the same schema map, gated by ad-hoc conditions and using JSON.stringify as a structural-equality proxy. That's INCIDENTAL-COMPLEXITY and EASY-NOT-SIMPLE — easy because each individual `if` block is small, not simple because the concerns are complected and the slot meanings change mid-traversal. The right shape is to compute the final schema as a pure function of explicit, named inputs (own properties, inherited properties, relationship-kind, extracted-ref-target) and assign once. Until then, the override-count doubling, the play.ts leak, and the silently-uncommented mini change are real ship blockers that the PR description hasn't surfaced.
